title: Electricity was never harnessed
premise: In 1831 Faraday's induction coils stay stubbornly silent, and the learned world files electricity away as a parlor trick. Civilization strides forward instead on gleaming steam, hissing compressed air, and mellow gaslight. It is a slower, polished world of brass valves, glass-roofed tube stations, ticking calculators, and long luminous evenings.

chain.event: Faraday's induction trials produce no usable current and are set aside as a curiosity.
chain.consequence: Investors and workshops redirect effort toward better steam engines, gas chemistry, and precision clockwork.

chain.event: Engineers perfect city-wide high-pressure air mains with standard brass valves.
chain.consequence: Factories run quiet air motors, and streets are laid with humming power pipes beside gas lines.

chain.event: The bright gas mantle and long-distance pneumatic tube post prove reliable at scale.
chain.consequence: Evening streets glow softly, and messages and small parcels glide beneath avenues, linking neighborhoods.

chain.event: Compact gear calculators and punch-card tabulators become affordable for shops and schools.
chain.consequence: Clerks, navigators, and teachers compute timetables and harvests mechanically, spreading skill with numbers.

chain.event: Hilltop wind arrays and river waterworks drive great air compressors and heat stores.
chain.consequence: Steam and compressed-air networks run on wind and water flow, steadying prices and honoring careful upkeep crafts.

chain.event: The League of the Steady Lamp promotes shared lamplight hours and slow evening gatherings.
chain.consequence: By 2026 cities prize calm lamplit plazas, public workshops, and lifelong training in air and clockwork crafts.

eras.caption: 1926 · Brass Pipes and Lamplight
eras.visualPrompt: Transform this scene to 1926. The buildings here house early steam workshops, pipe depots and gas-fitting halls in the region's own building tradition, with polished brass gauges, glass awnings and rows of warm street lamps. Pneumatic message posts and ticking shop clocks line the calm pavement under a soft evening glow.
eras.visualPromptIndoor: A snug workshop interior with gear calculators on long counters, glowing gas wall lamps and neatly racked brass tools for quiet evening study.
